featured.title: Guillermo Rauch · Vercel CEO
featured.summaryEn: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch raised a concern worth the whole industry's attention this week: the cost of AI slop isn't just bad code and bad PRs — it's that reading itself risks being discounted, because people are exhausted by a constant stream of low-quality, unverified AI prose. His example: a viral thread crediting a "perf improvement" to a compiler change, where the PR description itself contains the AI explicitly saying it was *not* the compiler — it was the algorithms and data structures. The poster never re…
featured.insightZh: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch 这周提出了一个值得整个行业警惕的问题：AI 泛滥的代价不只是"垃圾代码和垃圾 PR"，更严重的是阅读本身正在被贬值——当人们长期被低质量、未经核实的 AI 文字轰炸，会逐渐失去认真读东西的意愿和耐心。他举了一个正在疯传的例子：某个"性能提升"被归功于编译器改动，但那个 PR 的描述里 AI 自己就明确说了这不是编译器的功劳，而是算法和数据结构变了——发帖的人根本没读自己贴出来的内容。他给出的立场很干脆："Reject non-understanding"（拒绝不求甚解），AI 应该服务于理解世界、增强人类认知和创造力，而不是反过来制造理解的赤字。

featured.title: Peter Yang · AI 教程与访谈创作者
featured.summaryEn: AI tutorials creator Peter Yang filed three hands-on field notes this week. First, Claude's usage limits changed noticeably — "from barely usable to basically unlimited," a first-hand signal about Anthropic's capacity or policy shift. Second, he's building an app on Gemini's audio API to teach himself conversational Japanese: 10 lessons, 10 phrases each — exactly the kind of scratch-your-own-itch project that stress-tests whether a new multimodal API actually works. Third, he used Google's Antigravity for the firs…
featured.insightZh: AI 教程创作者 Peter Yang 这周是纯粹的一线手感汇报，三条都有信息量。第一，Claude 的用量限制发生了明显变化——"从几乎没法用变成了基本无限"，这是关于 Anthropic 产能/策略调整的一手观察信号。第二，他正在用 Gemini 的 audio API 做一个教自己日语口语的 app，结构是 10 节课、每节 10 个短句——这类"自己给自己做工具"的小项目，恰好是测试新多模态 API 真实可用性的最好样本。第三，他第一次用 Google 的 Antigravity（为了试新的 audio API），顺手吐槽了一句：反馈该提给谁？——新工具上手体验的真实摩擦点。

featured.title: Why Diffusion Will Win AI Inference with Stefano Ermon
featured.summaryEn: Autoregressive models are inherently sequential and memory-bound at inference time; diffusion models are inherently parallel — and in an era where compute and power are the binding constraints, that structural difference may decide who wins the inference market. Stefano Ermon spent his career at Stanford as one of the fathers of diffusion — the 2019 score-based generative models he developed with PhD student Yang Song became the foundation for Stable Diffusion, Midjourney, and most of modern image generation. He's now co-founder and CEO of Inception, a roughly 50-person, two-year-old company betting against the architecture every major lab has standardized on. His argument is concrete and hardware-level. The 2017 shift from RNNs to Transformers solved parallelism for *training* — process many tokens at once. But at inference, autoregressive models remain sequential: you cannot generate…
featured.insightZh: 自回归模型在推理阶段天生是串行的、内存受限的，而扩散模型天生并行——在算力和电力成为硬约束的时代，这个结构性差异可能决定谁赢下推理市场。 Stefano Ermon 是斯坦福长期任教的教授，也是"扩散模型之父"之一——2019 年他和博士生 Yang Song 提出的 score-based 生成模型，正是今天 Stable Diffusion、Midjourney 这一整条技术线的源头。现在他是 Inception 的联合创始人兼 CEO，一家约 50 人、成立两年的公司，正在用扩散架构直接挑战所有大厂押注的自回归路线。 他的核心论证非常具体，而且是硬件层面的。2017 年从 RNN 切换到 Transformer，本质上解决的是训练的并行问题——让模型能同时处理多个 token。但推理阶段，自回归模型至今仍然是串行的：不生成完前九个 token 就没法生成第十个。这种负载"根本不适合 GPU"——大部分时间花在把权重在内存层级间搬来搬去，真正做算术的时间极少，是典型的 memory-bound。而扩散模型在推理时的负载形态，跟训练时几乎一样：同时处理大量 token，正好映射到 GPU 最擅长的矩阵乘法上。他的结论引用了 Sutton 的经典论断："The bitter lesson is that the more parallel solution is the one that is eventually going to win." 这不只是理论。Inception 的 Mercury 模型已经在生产环境服役，质量对标 OpenAI 的 mini/nano、以及各家的 flash/haiku 级速度优化模型，但显著更快。一个真实案例：某语音 agent 公司原先要靠 Cerebras 定制芯片才能达到所需延迟，换到 Mercury 后，在普通 NVIDIA GPU 上拿到了同等速度——可用性更高、成本更低。因为没有 vLLM/SGLang 能跑扩散 LLM，他们从零自建了推理引擎，这本身成了护城河。Ermon 的判断是 OpenRouter 上大约 20-…

items.title: Thariq · Anthropic Claude Code 团队
items.summaryEn: Thariq, who works on Claude Code at Anthropic, offered a useful yardstick for how fast agentic coding has moved: roughly a year ago he posted one of the first threads about using Claude Code to make videos. He's explicit about what it actually cost back then — each one took a long time iterating with Claude, pointing out details that were wrong, correcting course repeatedly. Comparing that to today: "Crazy how far things have come." The value here isn't the flex, it's the concrete anchor point — work that required…
items.insightZh: Anthropic Claude Code 团队的 Thariq 回顾了一个很好的能力进步标尺：大约一年前，他发了最早一批"用 Claude Code 做视频"的帖子之一。他特意点出当时的真实成本——每一个作品都要跟 Claude 反复迭代很久，不断指出哪里错了、哪里不对，才能勉强做对。对比今天的效果，他的评价是"crazy how far things have come"。这条的价值不在炫耀，而在于它提供了一个有具体锚点的 agentic coding 能力时间轴：一年前需要人工逐处纠偏的任务，现在基本一次过。

items.title: Garry Tan · Y Combinator 总裁兼 CEO
items.summaryEn: Y Combinator President and CEO Garry Tan shared his current favorite debugging workflow: capy.ai plus GStack's `/autoplan`, running on GPT-6 medium reasoning, pointed at a real production issue. His words: "This is my favorite way to fix bugs now." Two details worth noting — he isn't maxing out the reasoning tier by default, which suggests medium is already the cost/quality sweet spot for locate-and-plan-a-fix work; and he's aiming the agent at production, not a toy repo.
items.insightZh: Y Combinator 总裁兼 CEO Garry Tan 分享了他现在最偏好的调试工作流：用 capy.ai 配合 GStack 的 `/autoplan`，跑在 GPT-6 medium reasoning 上，直接处理生产环境的真实问题。他的原话是"这是我现在最喜欢的修 bug 方式"。值得注意的是配置细节——他没有默认拉满推理档位，而是用 medium，说明在这类"定位+规划修复"的任务上，中档推理的性价比已经足够；以及他把 agent 直接对准 production issue，而不是玩具仓库。

items.title: Dan Shipper · Every CEO
items.summaryEn: Every CEO Dan Shipper ran an unusual creative experiment this week: he wrote a novelization of Plato's *Protagoras*, then had Opus 5.5 turn it into a movie — releasing scene 1 and scene 2 back to back. The interesting part of the chain — classical philosophical text → human-written novelization → model-generated visual narrative — is the division of labor: the human converts abstract dialectic into scenes and characters, the model converts that structure into audiovisual language. As an open, in-progress data poin…
items.insightZh: Every CEO Dan Shipper 做了一个方向很不一样的 AI 创作实验：他先把柏拉图的《普罗泰戈拉》改写成了小说体，然后让 Opus 5.5 把它变成一部电影，本周连续放出了第一幕和第二幕。这个链路——古典哲学文本 → 人写的小说化改编 → 模型生成的影像叙事——有意思的地方在于人类和模型的分工：人负责把抽象辩论转译成有场景和人物的叙事结构，模型负责把叙事结构转译成视听语言。对于"AI 到底能不能做长篇连贯叙事"这个问题，这是一个正在进行中的公开样本。
